extracted.intended_audience: journalism educators and news writing students (news writing instructors, journalism faculty)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and using a videotaped mock press conference to teach news-writing students how to cover press conferences, including student question preparation, on-camera etiquette, follow-up techniques, and post-event critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research questions in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Students in the public affairs reporting class researched the questions to be asked at the press conference, delving into a wide array of topics...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare questions across relevant beats (airport expansion, sewerage, mass transit, solid waste, library development, traffic/growth, earthquake preparedness, elections, image of politicians). Do not pre-brief the subject (McCarty was not told in advance), so questions test spontaneous source responses and student preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press conference etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Students discussed such things as press conference etiquette, follow-up questioning, topical and timely questions, use of 'light' questions..., note taking, and how to deal with cooperative and uncooperative sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and enforce standing when speaking, appropriate body language, orderly turn-taking, note taking, and respectful yet persistent questioning. Use the videotape to show examples of correct and incorrect etiquette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of follow-up questioning — extracting specifics and probing beyond initial answers (example: asking McCarty to name politically unsophisticated candidates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train reporters to ask logical, sequenced follow-ups that seek specifics; criticize missed follow-ups as lost opportunities for 'tantalizing news copy.' Praise returns to earlier topics when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical and timely questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Students were coached on asking topical and timely questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize current, locally relevant issues and craft questions that connect the source to recent events (e.g., post-earthquake stadium safety).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'light' questions to warm sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'light' questions designed to get the subject to 'warm up' to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a light or personal question to build rapport and elicit more candid responses later; plan light questions as part of overall questioning strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cooperative and uncooperative sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction on how to deal with cooperative and uncooperative sources; suggested future videotape with an uncooperative source to test students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train varied strategies (reframing, persistence, redirecting, follow-ups) and evaluate student adaptability when sources stonewall or dodge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wording questions to get past 'garbage' (be aggressive when needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: In live press conferences things move at a quicker pace and reporters have to be aggressive to be able to ask a question. They have to word their questions in such a manner that they can get past all the garbage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice concise, pointed wording; emphasize assertiveness and clarity under time pressure so important facts are obtained despite interruptions or evasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical sequencing of questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Students did not always ask follow-up questions in a logical sequence; jumpy order criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach planning of topical threads and transitions; encourage reporters to avoid random topic switching and to return to unresolved lines of questioning when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning to prior topics appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Returning to the recycling issue later was praised by the professional reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage persistence: revisiting earlier topics can yield important information and shows editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask for specifics/names where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to ask McCarty to name 'politically unsophisticated' candidates was pointed out as a shortcoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train reporters to push for concrete examples, names, figures, or documents rather than accepting vague generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Note taking was listed among the skills discussed in preparing students for the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize accurate, legible note-taking to capture quotes and details for later copy; use tape/stops to cross-check notes during classroom critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presence — stand when speaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Students commented: 'The students should have stood up when they spoke.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach physical conventions (standing to ask questions) to improve audibility, visibility, and professional appearance in live events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use videotape to pause and critique (instructional format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Playing the videotape back on a VCR permits the instructor to stop the conference at any point to point out good or bad things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design videotaped exercises so instructors can freeze, replay, and discuss moments immediately; editing can also insert good/bad examples for quick discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show both good and bad examples in critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Students suggested the reviewers should have shown more of the things that students did right rather than focusing on their mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance feedback: highlight successes as well as errors to model best practices and maintain learner confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include professional critique and classroom evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation segment by a staff writer and broadcast journalism professor provided praise and criticism; critique following the conference was as valuable as the press conference itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate expert reviewers to provide real-world perspective; structure critiques to address technique, phrasing, question quality, and sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism in production (set, actors, public figure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer arranged set with podium and press conference-like seating... the fact that Judy McCarty is an actual public figure and not an actress made the press conference that much more realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create realistic staging (lights, photographer, seating, podium) and, when possible, use real public figures to increase authenticity and student engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use as preparatory/scaffolding exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: The videotaped mock press conference is a good preliminary to having students do a press conference on their own and to critiquing a nationally televised press conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position mock exercises before live assignments; use them to build confidence, skills, and expectation-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss 'light' versus hostile questions and control
rubrics_metrics.description: The mock press conference can be used to discuss 'light' questions versus hostile questions, and ... who controls the press conference--the press corps or the source?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly teach distinctions between question types and tactics for regaining control of the agenda; evaluate reporters on ability to shape the event's focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of videotape for repeated viewing/time on task
rubrics_metrics.description: The videotape can be made available to students to view outside of class. Having the tape available to watch more than once allows more time on task for those who need it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access for repeated review; assess learning gains from multiple viewings and self-reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show nonverbal cues and emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: The tape shows the participants and their emotions, their exact words, their factual expressions ... things that can’t be as easily captured on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use video specifically to teach reading of tone, gesture and nuance that inform reporting and source interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mock press conference as a writing exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: The videotaped press conference can serve as a writing exercise for students who can cover the mock press conference as if it were a real one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign write-ups based on the tape to practice translating observed exchanges into news stories; evaluate accuracy, lead selection, and use of quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing for focused pedagogical examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A suggested future program: good and bad examples of questions would draw immediate comment from reviewers so that film editing would be conducted to allow for quick discussion of these examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing instructional videos, edit to isolate brief exemplary clips (good/bad questions, effective follow-ups) to prompt targeted discussion rather than waiting for entire sequences to play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness and reproducibility of instructional media
rubrics_metrics.description: This particular tape was done with a grant of $400... The production is now available to any faculty member in the University of California and California State University systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider budget, reuse, and distribution when designing instructional media; low-cost taped simulations can be widely shared as a common foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling through peer observation
rubrics_metrics.description: The mock press conference allows students to observe other students in action, a kind of modeling process...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer performance as a teaching tool: observing classmates exposes students to a range of skill levels and common mistakes, aiding learning-by-example.
